Name: Unit tests
Tooling: JUnit, pytest, Go testing, Vitest, RSpec
Pitfalls: Mocking everything → tests pass but real system is broken
Notes: Aim for sub-second suites; use real value objects, mock only IO boundaries.

Name: Component / module tests
Use Case: A component with its real collaborators (in-process)
Weaknesses: Slower than unit; needs careful seam design
Tooling: JUnit + Spring Slice / pytest + FastAPI TestClient / supertest
Pitfalls: Treating these as integration tests and skipping the next level
Notes: Useful 'middle layer'; favourite for hexagonal architectures.

Name: Integration tests (real deps)
Use Case: Real DB, real broker, real cache
Strengths: Highest fidelity for data layer & queries
Pitfalls: Sharing one DB instance across tests → ordering bugs
Notes: Use Testcontainers + per-test schema/database; great with Flyway/Liquibase migrations.

Name: Contract tests
Strengths: Catches breaking changes before deploy; decouples deploy timing
Tooling: Pact, Spring Cloud Contract, Buf breaking, schema-registry compat
Pitfalls: Treating as a substitute for E2E
Keywords: contract test pact buf consumer driven
Notes: Bidirectional contract testing (Pact 2.x) reduces broker dependency.

Name: End-to-End (E2E) tests
Use Case: Full happy paths through a deployed stack
Pitfalls: Trying to E2E every branch; not isolating test data
Notes: Limit to a handful of critical journeys; isolate per-test users/data; quarantine flaky tests.

Name: Property-based tests
Strengths: Finds edge cases random examples never would
Weaknesses: Slower; failure shrinking + reproducibility need care
Notes: Pair with classic unit tests; replay shrunk failures as fixed cases.

Name: Fuzz testing
Strengths: Finds crashes, OOMs, security bugs SAST misses
Tooling: libFuzzer, AFL++, ClusterFuzzLite, Atheris (Py), Jazzer (JVM), cargo-fuzz
Pitfalls: Treating fuzzing as one-shot, not continuous
Notes: Run continuously in CI (ClusterFuzzLite) with corpus persisted between runs.

Name: Snapshot tests
Strengths: Catches accidental changes; trivial to write
Tooling: Vitest snapshots, Jest snapshots, syrupy, approvaltests
Notes: Treat snapshot updates with the same review rigour as code.

Name: Mutation testing
Use Case: Measure how well your tests detect intentional bugs
Pitfalls: Running on giant scope without filtering
Notes: Run on changed files in PR; track 'mutation score' over time.

Name: Load tests
Pitfalls: Testing only happy path traffic mix
Keywords: load test k6 locust gatling jmeter
Notes: Run k6 in CI (k6 Cloud or self-hosted) on staging; track p95/p99 trends.

Name: Stress / soak tests
Use Case: Behaviour beyond capacity / over long durations
Strengths: Reveals memory leaks, FD leaks, broker backlog
Notes: Run a 24h soak before production; watch RSS, FDs, GC counters.

Name: Chaos engineering
Strengths: Reveals latent assumptions; turns 'might survive' into 'has survived'
Tooling: LitmusChaos, Chaos Mesh, AWS Fault Injection Simulator, Gremlin
Pitfalls: Doing chaos in prod without SLOs/error budgets
Keywords: chaos engineering litmus chaos mesh fis gremlin
Notes: Start in staging; graduate to GameDays in prod with go/no-go criteria.

Name: Smoke tests / synthetic monitoring
Use Case: Continuous black-box checks of prod endpoints
Tooling: Pingdom, Datadog Synthetics, Grafana Synthetic Monitoring, Checkly
Pitfalls: Treating synthetics as a substitute for proper SLOs
Notes: Wire into pager only when checks fail across regions to avoid false positives.
